title: Witnesses: ICE Agents Rammed Van, Salgado Was Parked When Shot; Agent Switched Guns
excerpt: Handwritten court statements from three passengers in Lorenzo Salgado Araujo's van contradicted the DHS account, stating ICE vehicles rammed them first, no agent was in front of the van, and the driver had stopped when the shot was fired. One witness alleged the shooting agent then swapped firearms with a colleague.
content:
On July 22, 2026, the Texas Tribune and Houston Public Media published the contents of sworn handwritten statements filed in federal court by two passengers in Lorenzo Salgado Araujo's van.

Witness Daniel Tirado Pantoja wrote: "At no moment were the agents in front of the vehicle" and that Salgado Araujo "had come to a full stop while the agents were shooting." A second witness, Jose Trinidad Rojas Pliego, said ICE vehicles rammed the van from behind and from the side before any shots were fired.

  • Tirado Pantoja also alleged that after the shooting, another agent arrived and switched guns with the agent who fired the shot—a claim first reported by Houston CBS affiliate KHOU and later confirmed in court filings.
  • The victim's brother, Victor Hugo Salgado Araujo, wrote that the gun was fired from the passenger side of the van, directly in front of his face.
  • Experts who reviewed available bystander video and photographs noted that damage to the driver's side of the van was inconsistent with the DHS narrative.
  • All three witnesses were being held in immigration detention and filed habeas corpus petitions arguing their continued detention was intended to suppress their testimony.

A federal judge subsequently ordered the release of one witness, Jose Trinidad Rojas Pliego, within 48 hours.
